thread:
irene: Proposal: layered package activation for air-gapped installs. base image + compact delta layers, each layer signed and optionally pinned. aim: smaller transfers, resumable apply, clear rollback checkpoints.

mike: high-level sounds good. how do we ensure activation ordering is deterministic across operator restarts?

irene: good q. plan is to attach monotonic 'apply-sequence' numbers to layers plus a small activation manifest that lists layer IDs + signatures + activation window. operator will persist last-applied-seq and only move forward. on restart it reconciles by comparing local seq with manifest.

sasha: what about partial failures mid-apply? if node applies layer N then crashes while applying N+1, we need idempotency and a clear safe-rollback point.

irene: operator should expose two stable markers: committed-seq (durable activation) and staged-seq (in-progress). we only advertise new capabilities after committed-seq. rollbacks are only allowed to previous committed-seq. staged-seq can be retried or aborted.

devops_ron: does this mean the package format needs a separate small "activation manifest" file? that adds extra bytes but simplifies UX.

irene: yes — separate activation manifest (json) that is small, content-addressed, signed. map looks like: {"base": <id>, "layers": [ {"id":"sha256:..","seq":42,"sig":".."}, ...], "activation_window": {"start_ts":...,"deadline_ts":...} }

mike: offline installers will want to validate everything locally. we should support a verify-only mode that checks signatures and seq gaps before attempting apply.

irene: agreed. CLI example (pseudo):
```
redwoodctl package verify --manifest ./activation.json --store ./blobs/
redwoodctl package apply --manifest ./activation.json --store ./blobs/ --dry-run
```

sasha: who signs the manifest? operator or a central signer? for enterprise customers we need to support customer-managed signing (KMS/HSM).

irene: auth model: publisher signs layers, ops team can sign activation manifests to gate rollout, or enterprise can enroll an external signer. we will support an allowlist of trusted signers per installation.

devops_ron: on rollback quorum: some sites want a safety quorum (e.g., must have 3 nodes confirm before moving committed-seq). do we plan built-in quorum or leave to operators?

mike: +1 for making quorum optional. default: single-node commit (fast). opt-in: cluster-quorum mode where operator collects ACKs from a configured set and only advances committed-seq when quorum reached.

irene: implementation detail: the operator will implement a simple two-phase commit for quorum mode: 1) stage layer on all members (staged-seq), 2) wait for ACKs, 3) commit. If timeout, can either auto-abort or continue based on policy.

sasha: observability: we need token-level metrics: staged_seq, committed_seq, last_ack_times, apply_latency per-layer. add per-layer digest and human-friendly label.

irene: yes — expose per-route traces in console + a compact audit log for on-prem: {seq, layer-id, action, actor, timestamp, outcome}. audit-bot should also be able to tail and push summaries.

audit-bot: got it — will emit a structured line to the audit stream when operator commits a seq: "audit:commit seq=42 actor=operator-1 layer=sha256:..."

mike: network constraints: for truly air-gapped customers we need a small seed bundle and a set of layer archives that can be transferred on physical media. how do we handle dedupe and resume?

irene: use content-addressed blobs with optional chunked transfer. the operator supports a local blob store with resume tokens. bundles can be a tar of blobs and manifest; if a blob exists, skip. we also support a "prefetch index" file listing required blob hashes so the admin can stage them.

devops_ron: edge case: operator crash during commit window where quorum thinks commit succeeded but some nodes didn't receive commit marker. we need self-heal.

irene: reconcile loop: on startup operator compares its committed-seq with leader (if quorum mode) or activation manifest. if divergence found, leader can coordinate re-sync or trigger a safe rollback to last known good commit. operators must support a manual override for emergency.

sasha: UX: admins will hate manual overrides. provide a dry-run remediation tool that calculates the minimal blob set to push to non-converged nodes and a suggested command to finish rollback/apply.

mike: does this approach interact with existing seed+delta protocols? avoids reinventing wheels but we need migration path.

irene: migration plan: new layered format can be produced from existing delta bundles by converting delta -> layer with seq mapping. operator will accept both formats for a deprecation window. add a compatibility shim in the loader.

sasha: security: include anti-replay nonces in activation manifests and short activation_window deadlines. prevents replaying old activation on fresh hardware.

irene: agreed. also recommend timestamped/expiring signatures for enterprise signers.

devops_ron: testing matrix: unit tests for seq idempotency, integration test for staged->commit transitions, chaos tests with mid-apply crashes, and a performance test for chunked resume under poor I/O.

irene: I'll update the RFC doc with these details: activation manifest schema, operator state machine (staged/commit/rollback), CLI examples, and migration notes.

sasha: thanks — can you also add a short runbook for "stalled commit" with commands to collect logs and perform safe abort?

irene: yes, adding runbook snippet in RFC. expected to land draft by EOD.

deploy-bot: deploy pipeline triggered: docs/rfc/layered-activation v0.1 -> reviewers: sasha,mike,devops_ron

audit-bot: manifest-signing-policy updated: allowlist size = 3 for enterprise accounts (opt-in)

mike: quick ack — will take a look this afternoon.

sasha: reading now, left inline comments.

irene: great — thanks everyone. leaving this open for one week for feedback before merging.
